Reply with JSON matching the requested schema and nothing else.

## Log, audit and escalate AI agent tool calls

### How it works
A chat agent is told to answer only from its tools, a calculator and a demo order lookup, with memory per session and intermediate steps switched on. After every reply a Code node runs deterministic rules over the run: a number in the answer that no tool result, question or earlier clean turn contains; an order, invoice or refund question answered without the lookup; instruction-like text inside a tool result; more tool calls than the policy allows; an agent that did not answer. A second Groq call judges whether the prose is supported. The rules decide FLAGGED on their own; the judge can only raise CLEAN to REVIEW, never clear a rule. Anything not CLEAN goes to flagged_answers and Discord, every tool call goes to agent_flight_log with the verdict, and the reply carries the status. Every morning a schedule counts the log, stores a digest and posts it when anything needs attention, including when nothing ran at all.

### Setup
1. Add a Groq credential to both Groq nodes and a Discord webhook credential to both Discord nodes.
2. Run Set Up Tables once: it creates the four data tables and seeds four demo orders, one deliberately poisoned. Every other node finds its table by name.
3. Ask the chat about order 1002, then about order 1004.
4. Tune Set Audit Policy: number length, ignore list, required tools, injection phrases. Activate the workflow so the daily digest runs.

### Customization tips
Swap the demo lookup for your real tools and point required_tools at their names. The rules are arithmetic and phrase lists, not judgement; the judge is a model that text can fool. A flag is a pointer for a person, not a verdict.

## 1. Create the four data tables (run once)
Each node creates one table with typed columns, or reuses an existing table of that name as it is. Every other node finds its table by name, so nothing is selected by hand. [Data table node docs](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.datatable/)

## 2. Seed the demo orders
Four sample orders are upserted by order number, so running this twice changes nothing. Order 1004 carries instruction-like text on purpose, to show the injection rule firing.

## 3. Policy and agent
Set Audit Policy holds the rule settings. The [AI Agent](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/root-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent/) is told to answer only from its tools and returns its intermediate steps; Simple Memory keeps the conversation per session. The lookup reads demo_orders by name.

## 4. Rules, then the judge
Earlier clean turns count as sources. Rules: numbers from nowhere, a required tool never called, instruction-like text in a tool result, too many tool calls, no answer, broken policy. The [LLM Chain](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/root-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.chainllm/) judge can only raise CLEAN to REVIEW, never clear a rule.

## 5. Escalate
Anything not CLEAN is written to flagged_answers and posted through the [Discord](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.discord/) webhook. Swap it for Slack or Gmail; the row is written first, so nothing is lost if the post fails. An agent or judge that fails is recorded, never dropped.

## 6. Log and reply
One row per tool call in agent_flight_log, or one none row, each carrying run id, session id, status and reasons. The reply repeats the status, the tools used and the reasons.

## 7. Daily digest: collect
The [Schedule Trigger](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.scheduletrigger/) fires every morning once the workflow is active; run it by hand to test. Log rows inside lookback_hours are counted per run: tool calls, flagged, review, clean. Zero rows is reported as no runs recorded, never as all clear.

## 8. Daily digest: report
The summary is stored in audit_digests. When anything needs attention, or nothing ran at all, it is posted to Discord.
